items.q: Why does the lymphatic system need movement so badly?
items.a: Lymph has **no central pump** and one-way valves. Blood pushes ~**20 L/day** into tissues; lymph clears the leftover **~3–4 L/day** toward the **subclavian veins**. "It's actually the **movement of your body** that creates the movement of lymph."

items.q: What daily movement target supports lymphatic flow?
items.a: Aim for **~7,000+ steps/day**, plus rebounding, swimming/treading water (skin shearing), and chores. All-day **micro-movement** matters as much as **150–200 min Zone 2** — desk/travel sluggishness is often lymph stagnation.

items.q: Can breathing move lymph when you can't walk?
items.a: Yes — **diaphragmatic breathing** (belly-out inhales) creates pressure at the **cisterna chyli**. Do **2–3 breaths** on waking, in the afternoon, or when desk-bound / on a plane.

items.q: Where should manual lymphatic drainage focus?
items.a: The **clavicle / subclavian region** is the drainage endpoint (right and left thoracic ducts). Use **light skin shearing → gentle tapping** on vessels — don't squeeze **lymph nodes** (professionals only; sore nodes can flag early sickness).

items.q: Why does poor sleep make your face look puffy?
items.a: During sleep the **glymphatic system** clears brain waste — astrocytes expand perivascular space ~**60%**; **side sleeping** (left or right) is best for efficiency. Incomplete clearance shows as morning **under-eye bags** and brain fog.

items.q: Do facial massage and gua sha have a real basis?
items.a: Yes when done as light **facial lymphatic massage** — outward strokes toward clavicle drainage zones. Gua sha/jade roller map to vessel mechanics if pressure stays light; deep tissue can briefly **push fluid** and cause transient puffiness.

items.q: Does drinking more water reduce puffiness or increase it?
items.a: Adequate water **paradoxically reduces retention** by supporting blood volume and lymph rate — roughly **16–32 oz on waking** plus **8–16 oz/hr**. Under-hydration impairs lymph flow and leaves fluid in the interstitial space.

items.q: How does cardio protect the heart via lymph?
items.a: Exercise promotes **lymphangiogenesis** — growth/remodeling of lymphatic vessels that innervate heart muscle, clearing cardiac waste and mitigating age-related inflammation — not only stroke-volume gains. Stack Zone 2 with daily movement.

items.q: What early warning should you notice in a limb?
items.a: **Minor limb swelling** can signal early **lymphedema** (often after cancer treatment destroys nodes). Management includes elevation, MLD, and compression; Stages 1–4 escalate if ignored.
